capabilities: Scan and organize skills, agents, commands, and rules across 15 coding tools at global and project scope
Enable or disable items by moving the actual files, symlink-aware
Install skills, agents, and Claude Code mods from GitHub with diff-reviewed updates and version history
Track usage, context cost, integrity problems, and prune candidates in an insights panel
List configured MCP servers read-only and jump to their config files
disambiguation: Not an AI assistant or chat plugin; it manages the skill, rule, and mod files that external AI coding tools read from disk.
extras: Desktop-only; it reads and writes files on disk and shells out to git for GitHub-powered discover, install, and update features. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
motivation: The author built it because skills pile up across tool-specific folders, copies drift out of sync, checkbox toggles do not touch the real files, and GitHub updates overwrite local edits blindly.
problem: AI coding tools each store skills, agents, commands, and rules in their own scattered folders, with no unified view, real enabling/disabling, or safe updates.

relations.evidence: Reads Claude Code's installed-plugins registry and Codex's installed plugin cache
Reads Claude Code and Codex session history (~/.claude/projects and ~/.codex/sessions)
queryable from Dataview or Bases like any other note

requires.name: an AI coding tool such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex whose folders it manages

summary: Library manager that scans AI coding tools' skill, agent, command, and rule folders so you can tag, toggle, install, and update them from Obsidian.
